newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Senator urges Clinton to move on trade bill.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Senator urges Clinton to move on trade bill.

text.p: Senate Commerce Committee Chairman John McCain, R-Ariz, said Monday that President Clinton needed to move ahead with trade negotiation legislation and take the lead in getting it through Congress.

Supporters of so-called fast-track trade negotiation authority, which would clear the way for U.S. officials to negotiate an expansion of the North American Free Trade Agreement to include Chile, are concerned that Clinton is waiting too long to propose legislation.

"It is time for the president to either fish or cut bait," McCain told reporters. Administration officials have said they are consulting with members of Congress to develop a bill that will win both Democratic and Republican support.

The proposed legislation has been delayed over a dispute between Republicans and Democrats over whether it should include authority to negotiate labor and environment issues. McCain said any legislation that include labor and environment would be a "non-starter" from the Republican majority in Congress.
"There is a great deal of mistrust on the Republican side about the influence of labor on this administration," McCain said.
But many key Congressional Democrats, backed by labor and environmental groups, have said that they will not support fast track authority that does not include labor and environment.

Fast-track would give U.S. trade officials authority to negotiate trade agreements without fear they will be later changed by Congress. Lawmakers could either accept or reject them, but not amend them.

Clinton said during a trip last week to Mexico, Costa Rica and Barbados said that he wants fast track authority to pass Congress this year, but that the first order of business would be to pass the balanced budget program.
McCain said that Clinton will need to make a strong push for fast track to get it through Congress.
"I hope that he will weigh in," McCain told reporters. "I believe that if he does it will be adopted."
